item.title: China urges non-regional countries to stop meddling in South China Sea issue: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday urged certain non-regional countries to respect its sovereignty and rights and interests and stop interfering in the South China Sea issue.
The Philippines and Australia recently signed a defense cooperation agreement, which the Philippine side claimed would bolster the Philippines' credible deterrent posture in the South China Sea to counter China's actions.
Asked to make comment at a regular press conference on Thursday, Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, said certain Filipino politicians, driven by personal interests, have been spreading false narratives about China, stirring up trouble, and seeking to rope in outside forces to back them up and make waves.
Such moves will only escalate tensions and undermine regional stability, Chen said.
"The South China Sea should be a sea of peace, friendship and cooperation. Stoking troubles and provoking confrontation are not welcome here," he said.
The spokesperson urged relevant non-regional countries to earnestly respect China's sovereignty and rights and interests in the South China Sea and cease meddling in the issue.
China's actions to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests are legitimate and justified, Chen said, adding that China will continue to take necessary measures to respond firmly to provocations and infringement activities.
China will resolutely thwart any attempt to destabilize the South China Sea, Chen said.

item.title: Premier Li: China ready to strengthen cooperation with ADB on regional development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Asian Development Bank (ADB) President Masato Kanda at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, the capital of China, November 26, 2026. /Xinhua
China stands ready to work with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to strengthen cooperation in areas such as regional integration, connectivity and emerging industries, and jointly promote regional development and prosperity, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Thursday.
Li made the remarks during his meeting with ADB President Masato Kanda in Beijing.
Noting that growing instability and uncertainty in the international situation in recent years have taken a toll on the Asian economy, Li said all parties need to further strengthen regional cooperation.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for building an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development, at last week's APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Li said, adding that China stands ready to work closely with all parties in the region to turn this inspiring vision into reality.
The ADB has long been an important promoter of regional economic integration, and China will continue to support the bank's relevant work, further elevate bilateral cooperation and jointly promote regional development and prosperity, Li said.
Against complex changes in the external environment this year, China's economy has stood firm under pressure and maintained steady progress, injecting much-needed stability and certainty into the Asian and global economies, Li noted.
China will continue to promote high-quality development, accelerate the unleashing of demand in its supersized market, deepen the integration of technological and industrial innovation, and maintain the strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, thereby contributing to regional development, he said.
China stands ready to work with the ADB to implement the new country partnership strategy, strengthen cooperation in areas such as regional integration, connectivity and emerging industries, improve the quality and efficiency of bilateral cooperation, and better achieve mutually beneficial and win-win outcomes, Li said.
Kanda congratulated China on its economic resilience and sustained growth amid global economic uncertainties, as well as its remarkable progress in fostering new growth drivers.
Noting that this year marks the 40th anniversary of cooperation between the ADB and China, Kanda said the two sides have made substantial progress in cooperation over the past four decades across a wide range of areas, including infrastructure development, poverty reduction, environmental protection and climate action, and have established a platform for South-South cooperation.
The ADB stands ready to work with China to effectively implement the new country partnership strategy, support Chinese modernization and the implementation of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), and elevate the partnership between the ADB and China to a higher level, Kanda said.

item.title: China unveils 2026-2030 services trade development plan, vows further opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Visitors browse the China Service Case Showcase at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) at Shougang Park in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Ju Huanzong)
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- China will expand the opening up of its trade in services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), according to a sector plan released on Thursday.
The plan, jointly issued by eight departments including the Ministry of Commerce, says China will refine the negative list management system for cross-border trade in services, expand market access in an orderly manner, and improve the standardization level of this sector.
The plan also aims to ensure the efficient, convenient and secure cross-border flow of factors including data, personnel, capital and technology. In particular, China will develop service infrastructure for cross-border data flows, deepen international data cooperation, and foster a more digital-friendly environment for trade in services, to facilitate the cross-border flow of data.
"China's opening up in the services sector provides vital certainty to global trade in services," said Yang Zhengwei, vice president of the Development Research Center of the State Council.
This opening up is expected to drive the growth of services trade, and the plan sets corresponding targets. By 2030, China's trade in services should achieve a better balance between imports and exports, according to the plan.
In the first three quarters of 2026, China's imports and exports of services reached 5,768.77 billion yuan (about 859.78 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.5 percent year on year, while the deficit in this sector came in at 1,225.97 billion yuan.
To boost services exports, the plan encourages professional service providers in consulting, accounting, legal, intellectual property and other fields to enhance their international service capabilities. It will also launch dedicated initiatives to promote exports in producer services, tourism services and cultural industries.
Meanwhile, China will expand imports of producer services such as R&D and design, resource recycling and environmental governance. It will also encourage imports of more high-quality consumer services, including healthcare, cultural performances and sporting events. In addition, outstanding foreign audiovisual programs and films will be introduced to Chinese audiences, the plan notes.
Li Bin, deputy head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, said China's services imports reached more than 620 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, covering travel, intellectual property, transport and business services, making China the world's second-largest importer of services.

item.title: China's high-standard opening up creates new opportunities for global cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Guests attend the 39th episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency. (Xinhua/Zhang Yuwei)
* Despite a complex external environment, China's goods imports and exports grew 20 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Imports rose 23.6 percent, continuing to outpace export growth amid China's ongoing efforts to advance voluntary and unilateral opening up.
* From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services.
* Beyond facilitating the flow of goods and production factors, China is steadily advancing its institutional opening up in terms of rules, regulations, management and standards, seeking closer alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules.
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- At Friendship Pass on the China-Vietnam border in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, an improved customs inspection system has cut the time needed to identify pests in imported fruit to 36 hours or less, down from three to five days.
This port handled durian imports worth 17.61 billion yuan (about 2.62 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of 2026, up 27.9 percent year on year, with China and Vietnam now jointly developing a smart border port to further facilitate cross-border trade.
These efforts reflect China's broader push to expand high-standard opening up and develop new competitive advantages, a theme explored in the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency.
A drone photo taken on Sept. 3, 2026 shows a view of the Qinzhou Port in Qinzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Cao Yiming)
BROADENING THE SCOPE OF OPENING UP
The country's trading partners are becoming increasingly diverse. In the first three quarters of the year, China's goods trade with Belt and Road partner countries rose 17.1 percent year on year, accounting for 51 percent of its total trade in goods.
Expanding into emerging markets has helped mitigate risks arising from slowing demand and mounting trade barriers in some traditional markets, making China's foreign trade more resilient, said Zhang Yan, a researcher at a research center under the National Development and Reform Commission.
In northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, trade with Belt and Road partner countries surged 35.3 percent year on year in the first nine months, according to Li Kaiyi, head of Yinchuan Customs.
To overcome the region's geographical constraints, local customs authorities have piloted a new customs supervision model for rail-sea intermodal transport, boosting logistics efficiency by more than 30 percent.
Local customs authorities have also helped wine producers resolve difficulties in obtaining certificates for exports to the European Union, with the value of Ningxia's wine exports to Germany and Spain more than tripling in the first three quarters of 2026, Li said.
Wooden barrels are seen at a wine cellar of Xige Estate in Qingtongxia, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Yun)
The potential for cooperation extends beyond the wine industry. Speaking in Ningxia, New Zealand's ambassador to China pointed to opportunities for technical exchanges between the two countries in wine production, livestock farming and crop cultivation.
China's opening up is also creating new opportunities for foreign investors. In Hainan Province in south China, the number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises rose 31.1 percent year on year in the first nine months of 2026, with new projects including a Siemens Energy gas turbine assembly base and service center, said Wang Fengli, deputy director of the Office of the Free Trade Port Working Committee of the Communist Party of China Hainan Provincial Committee.
DEVELOPING NEW COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES
China's advances in science and technology and the development of its digital economy are also creating new opportunities for international economic cooperation.
From drone-based crop-protection services for cotton fields in Central Asia, to the international expansion of domestically developed smart in-vehicle systems, more Chinese companies are moving beyond individual product exports to providing integrated technological solutions and services, Zhang said.
The country's exports of knowledge-intensive services grew 11.7 percent year on year to 1.2 trillion yuan in the first three quarters of 2026, accounting for 53.7 percent of its total services exports.
Opening-up policies are also helping develop new businesses in high-value-added services. In Hainan, for instance, bonded maintenance and expedited customs clearance can reduce aircraft maintenance costs for foreign airlines by around 10 percent to 15 percent, Wang said.
Staff members work at an aircraft maintenance base of Grand China Aviation Maintenance Co., Ltd. at the Haikou Airport comprehensive bonded zone in Haikou, south China's Hainan Province, Oct. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xin Yuewei)
Meanwhile, digital cultural products, including online literature, video games and online dramas, are another growing area in China's services exports, Zhang noted.
In Hainan's Chengmai County, a public service platform helps game developers overcome barriers to international expansion, such as cross-border network latency, regulatory compliance and payment settlement. The platform has attracted 125 enterprises and has more than 40 million registered overseas users.
Under the policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) on secure and orderly cross-border data flows, this platform provides dedicated data links, reducing the costs developers would otherwise incur in arranging such connections themselves.
DEEPENING INSTITUTIONAL OPENING UP
The Hainan FTP serves as a testing ground for such reforms. Following the launch of island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports increased from 21 percent to 74 percent, Wang said.
Vehicles bound for Vietnam are pictured after customs clearance at Youyiguan Port, or Friendship Pass, in Pingxiang City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Lu Boan)
At the regional level, the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol brings cooperation in the digital economy, green economy and supply chain connectivity into an institutional framework, moving regional cooperation beyond tariff reductions toward greater coordination of rules, Zhang said.
Greater openness also requires stronger risk management capabilities, Zhang said, suggesting that pilot free trade zones and free trade ports conduct stress tests in areas like cross-border data flows, financial opening up and cross-border services trade.
Looking ahead, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) sets out measures to further expand the areas and geographical scope of opening up in an orderly manner, promote innovation in trade, and attract and utilize more foreign investment.
"Regardless of changes in the international landscape, China will continue to counter external uncertainties with the certainty of steadily expanding its voluntary opening up," Zhang said, adding that China's high-quality development will create new opportunities for countries around the world.

item.title: China firmly opposes US's additional tariffs on China, other economies
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday that China firmly opposes the US Section 301 investigation under the pretext of "overcapacity," saying that the investigation is a typical unilateralist act that severely disrupts the international economic order and violates World Trade Organization rules.
Ministry spokesperson He Yadong made the remarks in reference to the US Trade Representative's recently announced findings of a Section 301 investigation into "overcapacity" and its proposed measures to impose additional tariffs on 14 economies, including China.
China urges the US to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation, He said, adding that China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.

item.title: Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries.
It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission.
In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station.
Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people.
Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago.
Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity.
For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people.
He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations.
Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship, opening Tiangong space station to first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
* China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani astronaut, into the orbiting Tiangong space station.
* The Shenzhou-24 mission, carried out by Chinese mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. Ali also became the first foreign astronaut to board Tiangong.
* China's manned space program has consistently adhered to the principle of peaceful utilization, equality and mutual benefit, and common development, while actively promoting international exchanges and cooperation and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind in outer space.
by Xinhua writers Li Minghao, Yi Ling and Quan Xiaoshu
JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani astronaut, into the orbiting Tiangong space station.
Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson for the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA), described the joint flight as a landmark achievement in bilateral cooperation as the two countries mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year, and an important manifestation of their traditional friendship.
China's manned space program has consistently adhered to the principle of peaceful utilization, equality and mutual benefit, and common development, while actively promoting international exchanges and cooperation and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind in outer space, Zhang said at a news conference on Tuesday.
UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said the United Nations welcomed the peaceful use of outer space and the international cooperation this mission represents.
Aboard a Long March-2F carrier rocket, the spaceship blasted off at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. About 10 minutes after liftoff, the spaceship separated from the rocket and entered its designated orbit. The CMSA declared the launch "a complete success."
The spacecraft completed a fast, automated rendezvous and docking with the front port of Tianhe, the station's core module, in about 3.5 hours. The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard Tiangong opened the hatch at 2:35 p.m. and welcomed the new arrivals.
The two crews then took group pictures marking the ninth space get-together in China's aerospace history.
After completing a short-term joint flight, Ali will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft alongside two Shenzhou-23 crew members. The other two Shenzhou-24 astronauts will stay in orbit for roughly six months along with Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu, who has already spent six months in orbit and will remain aboard Tiangong to complete a year-long stay experiment.
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua)
JOINT EXPERIMENTS
More than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission, covering space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine and new space technologies, according to the CMSA.
Four China-Pakistan cooperative projects in the fields of biotechnology and materials will be conducted during the Shenzhou-24 mission, and Ali will conduct an experiment on photosynthetic cyanobacteria, which was proposed by the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO).
The experiment is expected to provide a biological basis and data support for oxygen regeneration and biomanufacturing at future space stations and deep-space bases, said Chen Mengyun, who is in charge of international cooperation projects at the Technology and Engineering Center for Space Utilization under the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Another cooperative project, led by the University of Agriculture, Faisalabad in Pakistan, will expose 32 quinoa seed samples to the space environment outside the station for about one year to investigate their stress tolerance and longevity, with the aim of screening for superior varieties.
Describing Pakistan as one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change, Pakistani Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal said that the country needs smart and climate-resilient agriculture.
"The mission gives Pakistani scientists rare access to space laboratories, offering potential breakthroughs to boost productivity and climate resilience," he told Xinhua.
The other two experiments will focus on multilayer graphene-based hybrid composites and solar-heated self-healing carbon fiber composites, Chen said.
Pakistani Ambassador to China Syed Ali Asad Gillani said the four experiments in orbit will not only benefit Pakistani researchers, but also help advance the prosperity and development of all humanity.
China-Pakistan space cooperation spans more than three decades. In 1990, Pakistan's first experimental satellite, Badr-1, was launched aboard a Chinese rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center. More recently, China launched Pakistan's cube satellite aboard the Chang'e-6 probe in 2024 and placed a Pakistani remote-sensing satellite in orbit via a Long March-6 rocket in April 2026.
This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali.(Xinhua)
COOPERATIVE TEAM
To support the joint flight, the Chinese side prepared bilingual Chinese-English manuals, provided food tailored to Ali's cultural and dietary habits, and tailored training and ceremonial attire for the Pakistani.
According to Shi Yusheng, an expert with the Astronaut Center of China, the center devised multiple methods to help Ali master Chinese commands and terminology critical for spaceflight. Beyond basic language courses, Ali received intensive training in high-frequency spaceflight vocabulary and commands. Later in the program, he was also taught classical Chinese poetry.
"With tight timelines and heavy tasks, we focused on spacecraft operations, pressure emergency response, fault handling and scientific experiments, and conducted high-frequency joint training to ensure the mission's success," Tang, the Shenzhou-24 mission commander, said at Tuesday's media briefing.
Wu, the mission flight engineer, said Ali had worked diligently to learn Chinese, while the Chinese crew used English as a supplementary communication tool. Through sustained effort, the crew progressed from merely understanding each other to anticipating each other's actions.
Ali can now communicate with his Chinese counterparts in Chinese. He described mastering flight skills, learning Chinese and forging close bonds with his Chinese crewmates as key gains from his training.
Ali said China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time. "Now it is time to show this great achievement in orbit and send the world a message that we work hand in hand for the peaceful utilization of space," he said.
In an interview with Xinhua, the Pakistani ambassador to China described the joint flight as taking bilateral relations "from Earth to space," calling it a dream come true for more than 250 million Pakistanis and "an excellent model for South-South cooperation."
This image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Nov. 25, 2026 shows a group picture of the crew of Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 spaceships. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
MULTIPLE TASKS
The Shenzhou-24 mission's main objectives are to complete an in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, maintain routine station operations, conduct space science and application work, and carry out maintenance, public outreach and payload tests.
One of the highlights is China's first year-long in-orbit stay experiment. The year-long test will establish a new system for studying the human body in space, conduct interdisciplinary frontier scientific experiments, explore and answer intrinsic mechanisms of human adaptation and remodeling in a spaceflight environment, build a space-human-body research database combining macro and micro perspectives, and produce a batch of original outcomes, said Zhang, the CMSA spokesperson.
In addition, the test will further accumulate practical experience in astronaut support technologies, enrich and improve the major safeguarding systems for in-orbit health, work and daily life, and steadily enhance the astronaut residency support capabilities of China's space station, he added.

item.title: Why Global Visitors Are Flocking to Chinese EVs in Shenzhen?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
From automated parking and tank turns to ultra-fast charging in extreme cold, each technological breakthrough is redefining what's possible in the automotive industry. But beyond the technology itself lies something even more significant: China's innovation speed, R&D capabilities, and industrial strength.
From leading global EV sales to attracting attention from international industry players, China's new energy vehicle sector is making a major leap—from exporting products to expanding its technological influence worldwide.
One car reflects the rise of an entire industry. And what's driving onto the global stage is the strength of Chinese manufacturing and innovation.
